title: Absolute-Frobenius trivialization commutes with finite coefficient change
statement:
Let $p$ be prime and let $X$ be a scheme of characteristic $p$ [def-weil-scheme-characteristic-p]. Write $F_X:X\to X$ for absolute $p$-power Frobenius [def-weil-absolute-frobenius-scheme]. Let $u:A\to B$ be a unital homomorphism of finite commutative rings. Use the ordinary unbounded derived categories $D_R=D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},R)$ of constant module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules] for $R=A,B$, and ordinary derived scalar extension $T:D_A\to D_B$, $T(K)=K\otimes_A^LB$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. For every integer $b\geq0$, let $\tau_R^{(b)}:L(F_X^b)_R^*\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{id}_{D_R}$ be the canonical absolute-Frobenius trivialization of [lem-trf-absolute-frobenius-site], iterated $b$ times, with its constant-coefficient identification; put $\tau_R^{(0)}=\operatorname{id}$. Let
$$
c_{F_X^b,K}:L(F_X^b)_B^*(TK)\xrightarrow{\sim}T(L(F_X^b)_A^*K)
$$
be the inverse pullback coefficient comparison of [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback] (1), transported to ordinary constant coefficients through [lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-condensed-ring-constant] and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-scheme-ring-constant]. Then for every $K\in D_A$ and every $b\geq0$ one has
$$
T(\tau_A^{(b)}{}_K)\circ c_{F_X^b,K}=\tau_B^{(b)}{}_{TK}
$$
as morphisms $L(F_X^b)_B^*(TK)\to TK$ in $D_B$. No flatness or finite Tor-amplitude hypothesis on $B$ over $A$ or on $K$ is required. In particular $b=0$ gives the identity comparison.

proof.text: For each exponent b, compare the relative-Frobenius site isomorphisms selected by absoluteFrobenius_proEtale_trivialization_pullback for the two coefficient rings. Their first projections are both the b-fold Frobenius on the site object, and their second projections are its structure map. The fibre-product universal property therefore identifies the two site isomorphisms, including at b=0. This is the private helper frobeniusSiteIso_eq.

proof.text: Write R for ordinary restriction along the constant-ring map and P_A,P_B for the ordinary Frobenius pullbacks. The canonical comparison beta:P_A R -> R P_B is the adjoint transpose of the identity-on-sections direct-image comparison d. Under the A-pullback adjunction the adjunct of beta followed by R(tau_B) is R(eta_B) followed by d and by the direct image of R(tau_B). Naturality of d rewrites this as R(eta_B followed by push_B(tau_B)) followed by d. The section normalization for d is identity; the section-unit normalizations for tau_A and tau_B then give the same restriction along the inverse site isomorphism of Step 1. Faithfulness of sections and the adjunction hom bijection prove beta followed by R(tau_B) = tau_A R. This is moduleRestriction_trivialization.

proof.text: All functors in the restriction square are exact. Apply the already proved CategoryTheory.Functor.mapDerivedCategorySquareIso_hom_app_id (WeilConjectures.SixFunctors.ProEtale.FiniteCoefficient.Derived.RestrictScalars) to Step 2. Its descended square is by definition the inverse of proEtaleRingRestrictionDerivedPullback, and its identity comparisons give exactly the two proEtaleFrobeniusDerivedIso trivializations used by coefficientFrobeniusTrivialization. Thus the same restriction square commutes on the ordinary unbounded derived categories. This uses the exact localization API and needs no K-flat representative.

proof.text: Let T be derived scalar extension, left adjoint to exact derived restriction R. By definition the inverse of directImageScalarPullbackIso is the scalar-adjunction mate of the restriction comparison of Step 3. Expanding that mate gives T(P_A(eta)) followed by T(beta) and the counit at P_B(TK). Compose with tau_B. Counit naturality moves tau_B inside T R; Step 3 replaces beta followed by R(tau_B) by tau_A R. Naturality of tau_A moves eta past it, and the triangle identity reduces T(eta) followed by the counit to identity. Hence inverse(c) followed by tau_B equals T(tau_A). Cancel inverse(c) to obtain c followed by T(tau_A) = tau_B. The private helper scalarMate_trivialization proves this generic mate calculation. It applies directly to every b, without an induction or a flatness hypothesis.
